description: Dorling cartogram showing eight Australian states and territories as non-overlapping circles. Circle area increases with the selected surfing participation measure, with a minimum size for readable numeric labels.

usermeta.title: How Do States and Territories Compare in Surfing Participation?

highlights.count: NSW leads in absolute participation: 117,953 estimated adult surfers.
highlights.rate: WA leads in participation rate: 1.76% of adults.

interpretations.count: Each circle represents an Australian state or territory, arranged to retain approximate geographic relationships without displaying the original state boundaries. NSW has the largest estimated surfing population (117,953), followed by Queensland (63,787), Victoria (58,683) and Western Australia (43,496). These results partly reflect population size rather than surfing prevalence. A minimum circle size is used so all numeric labels remain readable; the smallest circles are therefore not strictly proportional in area.
interpretations.rate: Western Australia has the highest estimated adult surfing participation rate (1.76%), narrowly ahead of NSW (1.67%). Queensland (1.38%) and Tasmania (1.36%) follow. Compared with the participant-count view, the relative size of WA increases significantly, illustrating why population-adjusted measures matter. A minimum circle size keeps the smallest rates readable, and narrow differences between survey estimates should be interpreted cautiously.

sources.label: Australian Sports Commission · AusPlay 2025 state and territory tables (30 Apr 2026)
